items: EGX30 jumps 2.08% to 52,483 on Tuesday, a second day of gains, with EFG Holding up 6.75% → slower inflation and foreign buying of Egyptian T-bills lift sentiment.
Remittances rise 20.4% to a record $13 bn in July to September, and reach $38.2 bn in the first nine months of 2026 → the largest source of dollars for Egypt keeps growing despite the regional war.
Hotter US inflation and a hawkish Waller make a December Fed hike nearly certain → a higher US rate narrows the carry on Egyptian debt and lifts the cost of Egypt's floating-rate loans.
Foreign investors buy about $614.7 mn of Egyptian T-bills on Monday while selling stocks → the carry trade returns, which supports the pound.

Urban inflation slows to 12.7% in October from 13.9%, a nine-month low, while core inflation eases to 13.1% → the CBE's 20% deposit rate is now about 7.3 points above inflation (derived), giving it room to hold on 17 December.
Brent falls 5.85% on Monday and trades at $91.88 on Tuesday after Trump calls the Iran war effectively over → cheaper oil eases Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound.
EGX30 rises 1.19% to 51,415 on Monday, but foreigners net sell EGP 302.9 mn → local investors drive the gains while foreign money takes profits.
Egypt Aluminum's quarterly profit more than doubles to EGP 4.93 bn → profit grows far faster than sales, which supports the stock's valuation.

The government raises gas cuts to fertiliser and methanol plants to 33% from 20% and notifies Ezz Steel of a 30% cut, with no end date → Asian LNG prices jump about 36% in a month, so Egypt saves gas for power and defers five of 15 November cargoes.
Abu Qir Fertilizers falls 5.78% and MOPCO 5.85% on Sunday as the EGX30 slips 0.67% to 50,812 → the gas cuts hit output at Egypt's largest urea exporters just as urea prices rise.
Evergreen's Ever Eon crosses the Suez Canal on Sunday, the line's first transit in nearly three years → the return of another major carrier supports canal revenue and dollar inflows.

Brent falls 1.5% to $96.91 in Asia on Monday as Trump says new strikes on Iran are very unlikely while talks progress → a US land blockade is now in effect, but de-escalation hopes outweigh new shipping attacks.

Egypt's annual headline inflation eases to 12% in October from 12.8% in September, with monthly inflation at 0.6% → slower inflation after the CBE's 100 bp hike widens the real rate and supports the case for holding rates.
Goldman Sachs says the pound is more than 30% undervalued and sees it at 50 per dollar in 12 months → a top bank's buy call can draw carry-trade money back into Egyptian debt.
The cabinet raises export rebates by an average of 35% and covers up to half of freight costs to new markets → the EGP 48 bn programme aims to lift exports and bring in more dollars.

The US sets up a task force to cut Iran's land supply routes as more blasts hit Qeshm and two tankers strike mines near Hormuz → the war widens even as Qatar-mediated talks continue, keeping oil and shipping risk high.

Cabinet orders three months of spending cuts: government electricity use down 20%, vehicle fuel down at least 30%, and no new projects or car purchases → the state is cutting its own fuel and dollar needs, a sign of fiscal strain but also of lower demand for FX.

The pound ends the week at EGP 54.01 per dollar at the CBE, with the dollar down about 2.12 pounds (3.78%) over the week → foreign money returns to Egyptian T-bills, and one banker sees 50 to 52 if inflows last.
Brent ends Friday at $98.32 as oil futures post their biggest weekly drop since 2022 → Gulf exports recover and traders bet on a faster end to the Iran war, which eases Egypt's import bill.
EGX30 ends the week at 51,152.73, up about 4.9% from Sunday's close (derived) after three straight gains → the pound's rally and falling oil bring buyers back; market cap reaches EGP 4.05 tn.

stories.h: Israel readies for a possible attack on Iran as Tehran warns of wider retaliation
stories.what: Israeli media report that the security cabinet orders the army to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran. Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei says US-linked bases from West Asia to Europe would be legitimate targets. Tehran rejects a US plan to move its enriched uranium abroad and says no talks are taking place. Brent settles at $92.76 on Wednesday and falls 1.58% to $91.29 on Thursday morning as OPEC+ output rises and US crude stocks build.
stories.why: Talks through Qatar stall while Israel's caretaker government weighs military action.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping, the Suez Canal and regional risk premiums.
stories.eg: A new war would raise Egypt's energy bill and hit canal and tourism revenue.
stories.egx: Bearish for tourism and logistics if it escalates; markets are calm for now.

stories.h: Eastern Company's nine-month profit jumps 39% to about EGP 9 bn
stories.what: Eastern Company's net profit rises 39% to about EGP 9 bn in the first nine months of 2026 from EGP 6.48 bn, and net sales rise 11% to about EGP 32.72 bn. The stock rises 4.17% to EGP 35.00 on Wednesday.
stories.why: Sales growth and wider margins lift profit; Arab Finance gives no breakdown.
stories.eg: Higher profit can support dividends for Eastern's shareholders.

stories.h: EGX30 ends flat at 52,500 as small caps slip
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Arab Finance; StockAnalysis.com
stories.what: The EGX30 edges up 0.03% to 52,500.47 on Wednesday while the EGX70 falls 0.26% and the EGX100 0.15%. Turnover rises to EGP 11.79 bn and market cap reaches EGP 4.18 tn. Egyptians net buy EGP 110.9 mn and foreigners EGP 30.7 mn, while Arabs net sell EGP 141.6 mn. Abu Qir Fertilizers (+5.04%), Eastern (+4.17%) and QNB Egypt (+2.86%) lead the table.
stories.why: Investors take profits after two strong sessions; earnings drive single stocks.
stories.aff: Blue chips, small caps and fertiliser stocks.
stories.eg: Foreign buying of stocks resumes in a small way after two days of selling.
stories.names: Abu Qir Fertilizers, Eastern, QNB Egypt (up); EFG Holding, Fawry, Edita (down).

key.l: public debt target, per cent of GDP, by 2030

stories.h: Egypt targets debt of 69.5% of GDP by 2030 and opens a Red Sea plot to pay it down
stories.what: PM Madbouly reviews plans to cut public debt to about 69.5% of GDP by 2030 and calls for ceilings on public debt, external debt and guarantees. Decree 448 of 2026 lets a 2,700-feddan Red Sea plot in Zafarana, reserved for sovereign sukuk, also be used to reduce debt, without selling the land. Budget-sector debt stands at EGP 17.85 tn, or 83.9% of GDP, at end-March 2026.
stories.why: The government wants to ease debt-service burdens and free room for priority spending, Arab Finance reports.
stories.aff: T-bill supply, yields, Egypt's credit rating and the pound.
stories.eg: A credible debt path could lower Egypt's borrowing costs over time.
stories.egx: Neutral now; supportive for banks and the market if yields fall over time.

key.l: Banque du Caire's 3Q net income, year on year

stories.h: Banque du Caire's third-quarter profit falls 20% as provisions double
stories.what: Banque du Caire's net income falls 20% to EGP 4.17 bn in the third quarter as credit-loss provisions rise to EGP 1.09 bn from EGP 489 mn in the second. Nine-month income rises 4.7% to EGP 13.11 bn, or about 19% excluding one-offs. Deposits grow 17% this year to EGP 473.5 bn and the capital adequacy ratio is 22.15%.
stories.why: Higher provisions and an 18% rise in administrative costs weigh on the quarter.
stories.aff: Banque du Caire's first results since its IPO at EGP 5.30.
stories.eg: Higher bank provisions can signal rising credit risk after the rate hike.
stories.egx: Mildly bearish for Banque du Caire; the nine-month trend stays positive.
